name: Lentil bolognese
summary: A thick meat-free bolognese of brown lentils, mushrooms, carrot, celery and baby marrow simmered in tomato and oregano, served over wholewheat spaghetti.
about: A meat-free version of the mince and tomato sauce served over spaghetti, with brown lentils standing in for the mince. The vegetables are grated or chopped small so they melt into the sauce, and a batch freezes well for another night.
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring now and then, for 8 minutes, until soft and the onion is see-through.
Add the mushrooms and baby marrow and turn the heat to medium-high. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the mushrooms have given off their liquid and it has cooked away.
Stir in the garlic, oregano and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, until the paste darkens to a brick red and smells sweet.

Add the tomatoes, water, lentils, salt and pepper and bring to a bubble. Turn the heat to low and simmer, half covered, for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick enough that a spoon drawn across the bottom leaves a clear line. Add a splash of water if it catches.

While the sauce simmers, cook the spaghetti in a large pot of boiling salted water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the packet says, until tender with a slight bite. Keep a cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Taste the sauce for salt. Toss the spaghetti with the sauce, loosening it with a little of the pasta water if needed, and serve scattered with the basil or parsley.
prepNote: The sauce keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer; cook the spaghetti fresh.
